limits: No experiments of its own: all figures come from other work and none of the cited numbers are printed in the chapter text.
Hierarchical indexing, hypothetical questions and HyDE are described without measured gains; HyDE is said to need cost justification.
Context-length and embedder limits (100K to 1M tokens, 32K embedder) are as of 2025 and will date.
Code is a toy pipeline with placeholder logic (query + ' OR related_term', 'specific_keyword'); the repo is needed for the rest.
Formula for the hybrid score is an image, not in the text; alpha direction is the opposite of Weaviate's.
practices: Identify which pipeline step a failure comes from before choosing a module (Table 6.1).
Use reranking: retrieve many chunks, rerank with a second model, give the top k to the LLM (Reranking).
Reorder retrieved chunks so the strongest sit at start and end, alternating even/odd with wide top-k (Reranking).
Use hybrid search (BM25 + dense) with alpha around 0.3 to 0.5 for exact terms plus semantics (Hybrid search).
Use hypothetical questions at index time or HyDE at query time; HyDE averages five generated answers in some variants.
Keep references to the sources used for generation (Reference citations).
Route queries by access domain to avoid cross-domain leakage and latency (Query routing).
Benchmark before production; monitor memory, cost and network as well as accuracy (Scalability).
Protect embeddings like the source text; defend against prompt injection, poisoning and membership inference; use guardrails such as NeMo Guardrails or Llama Guard (Security).
Use stricter prompts to force the model to use context (Open questions).
